_: mandarin-fixes.json — every hand edit made to the nine Mandarin decks, and the ONLY place one may be made. Applied by .claude/decks/mandarin-fix.js, which is idempotent and whose --check asserts the decks still carry these. The decks' generator inputs (w26-*.json) are not in this repo, so they cannot be rebuilt: this file is the whole record of how the shipped decks differ from what the generator produced. Keyed by <deck id>/<headword>. Every entry carries a `why`.

hintsWhy: AUTHORITATIVE: this map is the complete list of `not X` blocks in the Mandarin decks, including the 104 pairs the generator itself produced — it is regenerated from the finished decks, so a pair that stops colliding loses its block rather than keeping one that points at nothing. The English → Chinese card's front is the gloss and nothing else, so two notes sharing one are a question with two right answers. These are the 251 PAIRS that had no disambiguator; each member is given the deck's own `not <other word>` block, the shape 104 pairs already carry. A group of three or more is not hinted — naming four of five answers on the front is worse than the ambiguity — and is given a distinguishing gloss in `notes` instead.

decks.whyFields: An idiom's gloss says what it MEANS and throws away what it SAYS, which is the picture that makes a four-character idiom memorable: 谢天谢地 is 'thank goodness' and it says 'thank heaven, thank earth'. The Literally line is added to the Chinese → English card, under the meaning.
decks.whyCredit: The decks' example sentences come from Tatoeba and carried no attribution — 60% of the 20,010 shipped sentences are verbatim in Tatoeba's own Mandarin-English pairs, and Tatoeba is CC BY 2.0 FR, which requires credit. Added to every deck's description, which is what the Collections page and the Studio show.
